text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Parliament passed on Tuesday evening the bills promulgating the Hungarian-Russian, the Hungarian-Slovak and the Hungarian-Romanian basic treaties, despite opposition objections.

- The Hungarian Television (MTV) Board of Trustees yesterday rejected a business plan submitted by MTV president Istvan Petak for 1997 and a plan to dismiss him was shelved because no agreement was reached on a new executive.
- Takarekbank closed 1996 with record pre-tax profits of one billion forints, up from 575 million in 1995, its AGM was told,
- More than 10,000 people greeted Hungarian President Arpad Goncz in the main square of Tirgu Mures on the third day of his visit to Romania.

- The Budapest Public Transport Company BKV suffered losses of 6.7 billion forints last year as the 11.4 billion forints contribution by Budapest City Council was insufficient to offset the loss of the state budget subsidy.
- Hungarian tourist will be able to stay in Austria for up to 90 days without a visa from June 1 instead of the current 30 days.
